# Independent audit: binary Jensen products and the full parity tube



## 1. Helly and arithmetic accounting

For a finite source, Jensen affinity preserves exactly which source points lie in each subset's convex hull, hence preserves every deletion-kernel test and the finite Helly number. Intersecting a source with one convex set cannot increase its Helly number: append that set to an infeasible family and then discard it from the selected certificate. The union bound follows by selecting one exclusion certificate for each source. Thus the actual-height-slice sum and the binary (2^r h(P)) bound are valid, including deficient affine rank.

The crosspolytope proof covers every critical subset. A subset containing the center and at least (m+1) vertices contains an opposite pair, so it is not in convex position. A subset excluding the center and containing at least (m+2) vertices has two disjoint opposite pairs, so the center lies in every deletion hull. The empty simplex supplies the matching lower bound. Filtering the affine half-integral height leaves (2m) exposed vertices. The equation (2u-\sum p_i=1) has a rank-(m) saturated affine integer lattice, whose projection is the odd-sum coset of index two; the ambient extra coordinate is not an increase of intrinsic integer rank.

For the ten-point gadget, the stated eight-subset is empty and in convex position. Its supporting (y=0) triangle excludes both omitted points; the selected seven old vertices remain exposed and (p_2) is exposed in that triangle. Products therefore give an empty (8^r)-vertex lattice polytope, while Doignon in (3r) coordinates gives the opposite bound. All (9^r) filtered product points are exposed vertices. The integer height slices have exactly (2^j7^{r-j}) vertices, giving the exact sum (9^r), rather than an assumed product rule for Helly numbers.

## 2. Exact source products and all caps

The graph singleton-fiber property at every coarse integer base survives coordinatewise products. The body is full-dimensional in (4r+s) dimensions and is exactly the convex hull of its fine mixed source. Coarse fibers are copies of (K) in fixed (s)-planes at their graph heights: intrinsic (H_s) mass is (10^rV), while full coarse ((r+s))-volume is zero. Fine intrinsic mass is (9^rV). No conversion between these different volume dimensions is used.

The fine lower bound comes from the center's own simplex fiber. The matching upper cover uses nonnegative integer exposure penalties with gap at least one away from the target, so coefficient two excludes all other fibers even at closed boundaries. This proves the upper bound for every candidate, not just fiber centroids.

For the coarse lower bound, the (5^r) diamond graph points are centrally symmetric about the selected graph base, with the same product simplex law in every fiber. The previously proved paired-tail theorem therefore applies to every nonzero simplex-coordinate normal, with all remaining coordinates represented by independent symmetric scalar noise. A zero simplex-coordinate normal is handled directly by closed symmetry. For the upper bound, the sum of factor penalties has exactly (5^k) zero bases when the target has (k) central coordinates, and positive integer gap elsewhere. Its canonical simplex caps cover the complete target fiber, giving the bound at every coarse candidate. Thus the exact depths are (\Gamma_s/9^r) and (\Gamma_s/2^r).

The Gamma comparison follows from the displayed strict second derivative of (\log\Gamma_t). The only equality case in the product comparison is (s=r=1). The fine source remains above its actual (4r)-integer-coordinate OC target.

## 3. Full-dimensional parity tube

The tube is an invertible affine image of (Q_m\times[-\epsilon,\epsilon]\times K), hence is compact, convex and full-dimensional. For (0<\epsilon<1/2), exact fine sampling removes only the central coarse base and selects precisely one integer height at each crosspolytope vertex. Coarse fibers have full ((s+1))-volume (2\epsilon V), whereas fine fibers have intrinsic (s)-volume (V).

At the coarse center, every scalar cap margin splits into the centered simplex variable and independent symmetric noise from the base and tube coordinate. Paired tails give the lower bound (\Gamma_s); simplex caps independent of both those variables provide a matching global upper cover. At every fine vertex, signed coordinate exposure isolates its canonical simplex caps. Own-fiber centroids give the opposite inequality. Therefore both claimed maxima and their ratio (1/(2m)) are exact for all closed ambient halfspaces.

The projected-law total variation is precisely (1/(2m+1)), with the stated supremum-over-events convention. It is not a statement about retaining that fraction of raw coarse Hausdorff volume. The fine hull is exactly the zero-thickness graph product and has codimension one in the original body. Its saturated base lattice has rank (m), with the same odd-parity index-two projection. The text correctly keeps this hull limitation separate from the exact-fine-hull diamond products.

## Verification

Both commands completed successfully:

- `work/math-venv/bin/python supporting computation verify_binary_filter_and_diamond_products.py`
- `work/math-venv/bin/python supporting computation verify_one_parity_condition_depth_loss.py`

These are scoped arithmetic/source counterexamples and relative bounds. They neither contradict OC nor establish a general retention theorem for varying fibers.
